series.title: Oxblood
series.lightNote: One key, one flag, no fill
series.blurb: Red in four weights: tulle, gloss, cotton and sky. One hard key and a black flag decide where each one burns and where it goes out.
series.brief: Evening wear for a fictional autumn collection. The only colour allowed was red, and the only rule was a single hard key from camera left with a black flag to cut the spill. Every frame asks the same question of a different fabric: what does red do when the light is this hard.
series.alt: red evening wear under a single hard key light

series.title: Bone
series.blurb: Everything pale: white floor, white wall, grey satin. The light has to be low and from the side or the garments vanish into the set.
series.brief: A daywear line in off-whites and greys. On a white set the garment disappears unless the light rakes across it, so these frames step the key around the set until the tailoring reads as a shape again.
series.alt: pale daywear on a white studio set

series.title: Black
series.garments: Feather, knit and wool, black on black
series.blurb: Black on grey, black on white, black on black. The garment only exists where the light finds an edge, so the light is the subject.
series.brief: Black clothing is photographed by what surrounds it. A pale ground gives a silhouette, a grey one gives texture, and a black one gives only the rim of light on feather, sleeve or hair. Five setups, one colour.
series.alt: black clothing against pale and dark grounds

series.title: Gilt
series.blurb: Warm surfaces that hold light: gold fringe, fur, pearls, chrome. The job is to keep them from turning into glare.
series.brief: Anything metallic or deeply textured either glows or blows out. The day was spent finding the soft, low key that lets fringe, fur and chrome keep their detail while still looking expensive.
series.alt: gold, chrome and fur in warm light

series.title: Stage
series.blurb: The last setup of the day is the dark one: a runway, a single light, and clothes built to be seen from a distance.
series.brief: Runway and show looks, shot the way the audience sees them: from far away, in the dark, with one light carrying the whole garment. Distance does the editing, and the frames stay loose.
series.alt: runway and sculptural looks under a single light
